A stupa is a domed religious structure, a type of megalithic monument found throughout South Asia. Stupas (the word means "hair knot" in Sanscrit) were built by Buddhists, and the earliest extant ones date to the spread of the Buddhist religion in the 3rd century BC. Stupas are not the only type of religious monument constructed by early Buddhists: sanctuaries (griha) and monasteries (vihara) were also prominent. But stupas are the most distinctive of these. Buddhist scholar Debala Mitra outlined four broad types of stupas found in mainland South Asia (cited in Fogelin 2012). The first (ancestral stupa) are those that contained the remains of the historic Buddha or one of his disciples; the second contain the Buddha's material possessions such as robes and begging bowls.
